name: flight-tracer
what_it_holds: Python package for fetching, processing, storing, and plotting flight data from ADS-B Exchange. CC0-1.0 licensed, 18 stars, actively updated (Mar 2026).
why_useful: More mature/maintained acquisition tool than the other ADS-B Exchange scripts found here; CC0 license means output data could be freely stored point-in-time. Useful base for building a repeatable airport-traffic nowcast series (gap #10) if the team wants to start collecting ADS-B snapshots going forward.
geography: Global (ADS-B Exchange coverage, configurable by user)
themes: Flight tracking and schedules: OpenSky, ADS-B Exchange, FlightRadar scrapers, aviationstack samples, airline seat capacity by route
why_all: More mature/maintained acquisition tool than the other ADS-B Exchange scripts found here; CC0 license means output data could be freely stored point-in-time. Useful base for building a repeatable airport-traffic nowcast series (gap #10) if the team wants to start collecting ADS-B snapshots going forward.

name: opensky-traffic-viz
what_it_holds: Python tools to load and visualize OpenSky Network air traffic data (OpenSky's REST/Impala historical database of ADS-B flight records going back to ~2019, covering scheduled and general aviation traffic globally). MIT licensed, 11 stars.
why_useful: OpenSky Network's underlying historical database (queried through this or similar clients) is one of the few genuinely long-run, free, global flight-position archives -- a route-level or airport-level flight-count series derived from it could serve as an airline capacity/traffic proxy for gap #10. This particular repo is just a viz/loading helper, not the data itself, so it is a pointer to the acquisition method rather than a dataset.
geography: Global (OpenSky Network sensor coverage, strongest in Europe/US)
time_coverage: OpenSky historical DB extends back to ~2019 (not committed in this repo; queried live)
size_hint: Tool only; underlying OpenSky database is very large (external, queried via API)
themes: Flight tracking and schedules: OpenSky, ADS-B Exchange, FlightRadar scrapers, aviationstack samples, airline seat capacity by route
why_all: OpenSky Network's underlying historical database (queried through this or similar clients) is one of the few genuinely long-run, free, global flight-position archives -- a route-level or airport-level flight-count series derived from it could serve as an airline capacity/traffic proxy for gap #10. name: dataset-flights-brazil
what_it_holds: Committed dataset from Brazil's ANAC (national civil aviation agency): anac.csv.lrz (compressed flight records, all registered flights in Brazil), airports.csv (ICAO codes, names, coordinates for every airport appearing in the ANAC records), and air_traffic.graphml (an airport-connection graph weighted by flight counts). 39 commits.
why_useful: Direct, free, committed domestic flight-volume data for Brazil -- fills part of gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, specifically Brazil, alongside the Embratur/IBGE sources already flagged) and could proxy inbound tourism/business-travel intensity to Brazilian Airbnb markets.
size_hint: compressed CSV (lrzip) of unspecified but apparently substantial row count + airport list + graph file
time_coverage: not stated in README; spans ANAC's public flight-record history
last_activity: 39 commits, exact last-commit date not surfaced
themes: Flight tracking and schedules: OpenSky, ADS-B Exchange, FlightRadar scrapers, aviationstack samples, airline seat capacity by route
why_all: Direct, free, committed domestic flight-volume data for Brazil -- fills part of gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, specifically Brazil, alongside the Embratur/IBGE sources already flagged) and could proxy inbound tourism/business-travel intensity to Brazilian Airbnb markets.

name: openflights
what_it_holds: The classic OpenFlights database: airports.dat (~7,000+ airports worldwide, IATA/ICAO/coords), airlines.dat (~6,000 airlines), routes.dat (~67,000 route pairs, i.e. which airline flies which city pair -- no seat/frequency counts, just route existence). Static snapshot, last meaningfully updated circa 2014, but still the standard free global route-network reference (confirmed via the flightdelay-dbt-warehouse repo, which cites OpenFlights airline reference at 6,162 rows).
why_useful: Gives a free global city-pair route-network topology that can be combined with T-100/other capacity sources or used as a static baseline for which international gateways connect to which Airbnb-heavy markets; AGPL-3.0 licensed code repo, data itself widely mirrored.
size_hint: 3 .dat files, tens of thousands of rows combined
time_coverage: static snapshot, last substantive update ~2014 (stale for current capacity, still useful as network topology)
license: AGPL-3.0 for code; data conventionally treated as open/attributable
last_activity: low -- largely dormant, occasional maintenance commits
themes: Flight tracking and schedules: OpenSky, ADS-B Exchange, FlightRadar scrapers, aviationstack samples, airline seat capacity by route
wildcard: a quant building a KPI nowcast for a consumer-internet compa
why_all: Gives a free global city-pair route-network topology that can be combined with T-100/other capacity sources or used as a static baseline for which international gateways connect to which Airbnb-heavy markets; AGPL-3.0 licensed code repo, data itself widely mirrored.

Not a KPI time series but a clean route-network reference table; useful as a join key / weighting scheme to turn airline capacity or airport-passenger stats (gap #10) into a regional travel-intensity index by market, cheaper than building an airport list from scratch.

name: euctrl-pru/airport-dashboard
what_it_holds: Dashboard application for airport performance monitoring, part of the official EUROCONTROL PRU org; likely consumes PRU data APIs rather than storing a standalone dataset (not independently verified - README not fetched due to budget).
why_useful: Could point to airport-level throughput metrics (delays, movements) that correlate with regional travel activity in Europe; needs closer inspection to confirm data vs. dashboard-only.
